text.tspan: Key Vault: architecture, security model & flows

Self-hosted team secrets manager. Express 5 + PostgreSQL 16 + React SPA. Server-side envelope encryption (AES-256-GCM) rooted in an ejson keypair. Sections: A system architecture, B key hierarchy, C data model, D
flows 1-10, E RBAC, F audit chain, G threat model.
Plaintext key or secret IN MEMORY only
Root of trust: ejson private key
Arrows are bound to shapes: drag a box and its arrows and labels follow. Regenerate with: python3 docs/tools/gen_excalidraw.py
Container: node:24-alpine, non-root, read-only rootfs, cap_drop ALL, no-new-privileges
TRUST BOUNDARY: vault server host (trusted; holds KEK in memory)
One Node 24 process serves the SPA and the API from the same origin. Secrets for the server itself come only from the ejson file, decrypted in memory at boot.

Each environment is a separately keyed vault. Only ciphertext is persisted; plaintext keys live in process memory and are zeroed after use.
NaCl box = Curve25519 + XSalsa20-Poly1305; one ephemeral
keypair per session, fresh 24-byte nonce per value.

Organization (single instance) → Project → Environment (own DEK, own members) → Secret → SecretVersion. Blue = holds ciphertext or hashes only.

Per-environment roles viewer < editor < owner. Admin is a separate global flag that grants NO implicit secret access.
Reveal value (audited; re-auth in protected envs)
• Admin self-grant allowed but audited (member.admin_self_grant) and owners alerted
• Protected env (prod by default): editors confirm each change with the env slug; viewers need recent MFA to reveal; others
file an AccessRequest for time-boxed access
• The last owner of an environment cannot be removed
• Service tokens: scope read → JSON / ejson pull; scope export → ejson only
Every auth event, reveal, change, export, import, token use, membership change and rotation is appended. Secret values are never written to meta.
hash(n) = SHA-256( prevHash(n) + canonicalJSON({ action, actorType, actorId, projectId, envId, secretId, ip, userAgent, meta, at }) )
canonicalJSON = sorted keys, no whitespace. Genesis prevHash = 64 zeros.

See SECURITY.md for the full model and scope.
Every value is AES-256-GCM ciphertext; the KEK is not in the DB; TOTP seeds encrypted; tokens, invites
ejson files hold only ciphertext + public key; private key never committed or baked into the image
GCM tag + AAD binds ciphertext to env, secret, version and key name
__Host-, HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict; 15 min idle / 8 h absolute; re-auth for sensitive ops;
csrf-sync synchroniser token on every non-GET + SameSite=Strict
Argon2id, mandatory MFA, 10/min/IP rate limit, 15 min lockout after 5 failures, breached-password
No implicit secret access; self-grant audited and owners alerted
Strict CSP (script-src 'self', frame-ancestors 'none'), React escaping, no dangerouslySetInnerHTML
pino redaction, no values in audit meta, Cache-Control: no-store, values only via POST /reveal, one
Masked by default, re-mask and clipboard clear after 30 s, idle lock
sha256-only storage, scopes, expiry, revocation, per-use audit + lastUsedAt
Per-env DEK with encCount, auto-rotation at 2^30
Loss of the ejson private key
AVAILABILITY RISK: back the key up separately and offline. Without it the data is unrecoverable
ACCEPTED RISK of server-side encryption; reduced by KEK/DEK rotation, least-privilege hosting,
